{{Quote|Join us and you can continue to transact business in Confederacy spheres—through Falleen, Ruusan, all the way to the Tion sectors.|[[Count]] [[Dooku]] attempts to convince [[Governor]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] of [[Eriadu]] to join the Separatists|<ref name="Tarkin" />}}
'''Ruusan''' was a [[planet]]<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''</ref> located in the [[Ruusan system]]<ref name="Episode Gallery" /> within the [[Teraab sector]]<ref name="BMF 98" /> of [[the galaxy]]'s [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]]<ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> that was [[orbit]]ed by three [[moon]]s.<ref name="Duel of the Droids" /><ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> It was positioned at the coordinates P-11<ref name="The Force Awakens Beginner Game" /> of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]].<ref name="Rebel Dossier">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref>

Ruusan was the site of the final [[defeat of the Sith]]<ref name="Helmet Collection 29">{{HelmetCollectionCite|29|Databank A-Z}}</ref> at the end of the [[Jedi-Sith War]].<ref name="SWP">''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]''</ref> It was host to a number of ancient relics, strewn across its many historical [[Battle on Ruusan|battlefields]].<ref name="Smuggler's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Smuggler's Guide]]''</ref> Following the defeat of the Sith, [[Form II]] "Makashi" fell out of fashion in the [[Jedi Order]] and was gradually seen as a mere [[Jedi training|training exercise]].<ref name="Lightsabers and Jedi Equipment">{{EncyclopediaCite|Lightsabers and Jedi Equipment}}</ref> A room in the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]] was decorated with stained [[glass]] windows, one of which depicted one of the battles on Ruusan.<ref name="Lightsaber Lost">{{TCW|Lightsaber Lost}}</ref>

During the [[Separatist Crisis]], it was aligned with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]],<ref name="Tarkin" /> and, during the [[Clone Wars]], [[Ruusan 2|one]] of its moons was the location of [[Skytop Station]], a secret Separatist [[listening post]].<ref name="Duel of the Droids" /> The former [[Pirate Queen]] [[Maz Kanata]] marked it as a point of interest on a map she included in the [[book]] that would become known as the ''[[Smuggler's Guide]]''.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />

[[Beilert Valance]], [[T'onga]], and many other [[bounty hunter]]s visited and fought at Ruusan while searching for [[Nakano Lash]], who had hidden on the world with [[Cadeliah]], the heir to the [[Unbroken Clan]] and [[Mourner's Wail Syndicate|Mourner's Wail]] crime syndicates.<ref name="Bounty Hunters 4">[[Bounty Hunters 4|''Bounty Hunters'' 4]]</ref><ref name=" Bounty Hunters 5">[[Bounty Hunters 5|''Bounty Hunters'' 5]]</ref> T'onga was injured by [[Boba Fett]] in orbit, but was healed by a [[Unidentified human (Ruusan)|man]] who owned a [[Furball|nexu]]. T'onga's wife [[Losha Tarkon]] found her there, and the two set off from Ruusan together with the nexu to avenge Lash.<ref name=" Bounty Hunters 9">[[Bounty Hunters 9|''Bounty Hunters'' 9]]</ref><ref name=" Bounty Hunters 10">[[Bounty Hunters 10|''Bounty Hunters'' 10]]</ref>

The planet shared its name with the [[Ruusan Reformations]], an event of governmental reform in the [[Galactic Republic]],<ref name="Collapse of the Republic">''[[Collapse of the Republic]]''</ref> and the [[Ruusan Armistice]], a truce that led to the creation of new standards of humane behavior in wartime.<ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Ruusan made its first appearance in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in "[[Duel of the Droids]]," the seventh episode of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''{{'}} [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]],<ref name="Duel of the Droids" /> which originally aired on [[November 14]], [[2008]].<ref name="Duel of the Droids air date">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/duel-of-the-droids-episode-guide|text="Duel of the Droids" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}}</ref>

[[File:Jedi_Temple_stained_glass_concept_art.png|thumb|right|250px|Jedi Temple stained glass concept art in ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two'']]
Ruusan appeared in the artwork by [[Wayne Lo]] titled "Unused Jedi Temple mosaic" for the [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series. It was included in the production journal of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two]]''. The concept art also depicted [[Valenthyne Farfalla]] leading the [[Army of Light/Legends|Army of Light]], [[Jedi Lord|Lord]] [[Hoth (Jedi Lord)|Hoth]] and the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Pernicar]].<ref name="TCW CS2">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]]</ref> Parts of the mosaic can be seen, which includes Ruusan, in a [[Unidentified veranda (Jedi Temple)|room]] in "[[Lightsaber Lost]]," the eleventh episode of the second season of the series.<ref name="LL">{{TCW|Lightsaber Lost}}</ref>

The planet was originally created for the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'', where it played a prominent role as the location of the powerful [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] known as the [[Valley of the Jedi]].<ref name="Jedi Knight">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref> In Legends, it was later revealed as the site of the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|final battle]] of the [[New Sith Wars]],<ref name="TEG">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> which served as the catalyst for the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] that reorganized the [[Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Rule of Two">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>

The [[2017]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' mistakenly depicts Ruusan using an image of the Ruusan moon.<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" />
